question: Player A controls Leovold, Emissary of Trest and Notion Thief. Player B casts Brainstorm. What happens?
answer: Player A draws 3 cards, then Player B puts 2 cards from their hand on top of their library. Cards are drawn one at a time. (121.2) The first card draw from Brainstorm is the first card that Player B would draw this turn, so Leovold, Emissary of Trest doesn't affect it and Notion Thief causes Player A to draw a card instead. Player B still hasn't drawn a card this turn, so the same process is repeated with the next two draws. Then Player B finishes resolving Brainstorm.

question: Player A controls a Blood Tyrant that they took control of from Braylen using Traitorous Instinct. Player A has 1 life. Player B casts Char targeting Player A. After it resolves and Player A loses the game, will Blood Tyrant get the +1/+1 counters?
answer: No. As Player A loses the game, the effect granting them control of Blood Tyrant ends, and it returns to Braylen. (800.4a) "Loses the game" triggers use the game state immediately before they triggered to determine how that trigger is handled. (603.10, 603.10f) Since Player A controlled Blood Tyrant right before losing the game, the trigger would be placed onto the stack under their control. However Player A is no longer in the game when the trigger would be placed onto the stack, so it never is. (800.4d)

question: Player A and Player B each control a Death's Shadow. Player A has 6 life and Player B has 9. Player A attacks with their Death's Shadow, and Player B blocks it with theirs. Player A casts Temur Battle Rage targeting their Death's Shadow. If Player B is dealt as much damage as possible during combat, what is their resulting life total?
answer:
1. In the first combat damage step, Player A can assign 6 damage to Player B's Death's Shadow and 1 damage to Player B. (702.19b) Player B's Death's Shadow will die before the second combat damage step (510.3, 704.3, 510.4), at which point Player B will be dealt another 7 damage. (702.19d)

Assigning any other amount of damage to Death's Shadow in the first combat damage step would result in less total damage dealt to Player B. In particular, assigning any less than 6 damage to Player B's Death's Shadow in the first combat damage step will result in it surviving and being able to block more damage in the second combat damage step.
